Manifest v0.2.1-rc.2; three exports (. host, ./client, ./src/*), dsh.client.platform=web, publishes lib/devtools/** but no scripts/.
Solution-style config referencing tsconfig.host.json and tsconfig.client.json.
Host+Worker project; explicit 130-entry files array is what enforces the face separation (checked by layout.host.spec.ts).
Browser-client project; lists Client+shared sources and seven client-UI package references.
Build config for lib/index.js, lib/client.js and lib/worker.js; neverBundle keeps ws external; build:done hook runs buildDevtools().
Published-profile overlay inserting the built plugin at ./lib/index.js.
Source overlay for pnpm run demo:inspector inserting ./src/index.ts through the CLI tsx loader.
Two English strings (title, description) for the composer Inspector slot.
Two Chinese strings for the composer Inspector slot.
36x36 SVG package icon (lens over a data panel) with a mask and two gradients.
12-line same-origin bootstrap: derives the authenticated cdp WebSocket endpoint from the page URL, preserving the deployment prefix.
Vendored Chromium BSD-3 license (27 lines) republished with the mirrored DevTools frontend; read in full, no mechanism.
Host package entry: re-exports the plugin, declares ctx.inspector on Cordis Context, defines the schemastery Config whose every default comes from resolveInspectorOptions().

Host Cordis plugin: registers the bootstrap route BEFORE starting the Worker, serves the mirrored DevTools frontend, proxies the CDP upgrade, provides ctx.inspector, opens Chrome on --inspect; degrades only on the ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM code.
One-line re-export of ./plugin.ts as the Host entry.
Host controller: resolves and cross-validates options, spawns the Worker (built .js or a tsx data: bootstrap), creates the Host source, installs fetch capture, aggregates shutdown failures.
Worker failure containment: the error listener is never removed, waitForReady races ready/error/exit, stop() terminates and throws on timeout.
Host source over the MessagePort: a malformed frame closes the source rather than being ignored; frames for another generation are dropped.
Microtask-coalesced batching with at most ONE in-flight batch; the acknowledgement sequence must match exactly or it throws.
Host-side query bridge binding the shared InspectorQueryConnection to the MessagePort.
Routes Worker frames to Host lifecycle handlers and rejects Client-only commands with an explicit reason.
globalThis.fetch capture wrapper: clones request/response bodies, keeps the wrapper Request reachable so a caller abort still reaches native fetch, refuses an accessor fetch.
Creates the Host source descriptor (host-<uuid> id, fresh generation, performance.timeOrigin).
One-line re-export of the shared publishCordisTree for the Host face.
Declares that the Host has NO source-bridge capabilities (the Worker attaches to Host V8 directly).
Rejects a misrouted Client Runtime command on the Host bridge.
Rejects a misrouted Client Console control frame on the Host bridge.
Rejects a misrouted Client Sources request on the Host bridge.
Declares no Host debugger source-bridge capability.
Declares no Host CPU-profiler source-bridge capability.
Declares no Host heap-profiler source-bridge capability.
HostCdpBridgeUnavailableError: the single error type for "use the Worker's native inspector session instead".
Rejects an object operation that must use the Worker-owned native inspector session.
Rejects a property request that must use the Worker-owned native inspector session.
One stable sentence every Host bridge rejection quotes.

Browser Client plugin: claims a tab identity, opens the ingest WebSocket, publishes the Cordis tree, mounts the bottom panel; rejects startup on bad bootstrap/registration but only warns on transport failure.
One-line re-export of the Client plugin entry.
Starts the browser transport, claiming the tab identity before the socket and releasing the claim on failure.
Reconnecting browser source: size-checks every inbound frame before parsing, pagehide suspends and pageshow reconnects with the same logical id, and only the close event owns reconnection.
One bounded-backoff timer with full-jitter delay in the upper half of the window; backoff resets on Worker acceptance.
Buffered Client publisher that throttles on socket.bufferedAmount and survives reconnects with a full state replacement.
Routes the twelve Worker-to-Client frame families with an assertNever default.
Client-side query bridge bound to the active WebSocket generation.
Fallback label "Client" for an untitled page.
Tab identity claimed with a Web Lock so a duplicated live tab mints a new id; each transport generation gets a fresh id.
One-line re-export of the shared publishCordisTree for the Client face.
Client network topics are currently an empty list (browser fetch capture not implemented).
Assembles the Client source's advertised capabilities from the per-domain capability functions.
Browser Runtime executor: response handles stay PROVISIONAL until the Worker acknowledges, and a cancellation rolls back exactly the failing request's allocations.
Per-session live-object table and CDP RemoteObject serializer; attaches a Cordis semantic reference to recognised objects.
Lazy property enumeration that never invokes getters; the prototype walk is bounded by maxProperties and a visited set.
Transparent console/error observer; captures in a microtask so stack frames point at the caller and never affects the original call.
Read-only catalog of the Inspector's own bundle; the map URL is only known after the source is read, so a map-first read loads the source first.
Parses V8- and Firefox-style stack text, decrementing line/column to CDP's 0-based convention.
ClientRuntimeExecutionError: the typed transport failure, distinct from an evaluated JavaScript exception.
Declares browser-side active debugging unsupported (no pause-safe page agent yet).
Declares browser CPU profiling unsupported.
Declares browser heap profiling unsupported.
Bottom panel: three-state store (unopened/visible/hidden) so the iframe mounts once and stays mounted while collapsed; close restores focus only if the opener is connected.
Pointer-captured resize divider clamped to 20-80% viewport height, with Arrow/Home/End keyboard support and lostpointercapture handled.
Forwards the panel shortcut into the iframe, reading the EFFECTIVE binding each keydown; composing/consumed/AltGraph events are left inside DevTools.
Five panel strings in zh/en plus the LocaleNamespaceMap augmentation for inspectorPanel.
Panel styles: flex column sized by the --inspector-height custom property, 6px absolutely-positioned resize strip.
Five-line ambient declaration for *.module.css imports.
Public export surface of the environment-independent models.
Lossless-JSON model: rejects NaN, -0, undefined, cycles, exotic arrays, Dates, symbol keys, non-enumerable and accessor properties so values survive structured clone and JSON alike.
Exact-field readers: exactKeys walks Reflect.ownKeys, so a symbol key is an unknown field too.
Branded-identifier constructor shared by every layer (1-256 characters).
Disposers run in reverse acquisition order with the transport close appended last; every failure is collected into one AggregateError.
InspectorService facade shared by the Host and Client faces: publish plus a cordis reader.
Bootstrap route constants and the Client-selection reader, which THROWS on a repeated selector rather than opening an unfiltered connection.
INSPECTOR_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 0; pre-release peers reject every other version.
Two-line re-export of json.ts and validation.ts under a bridge-facing name.
Two-line re-export of ../validation.ts under a bridge-facing name.
The seven branded identifier roles of the bridge (source, generation, runtime/source session and request, remote-object handle).
Transport-independent publisher interfaces plus the abstract InspectorSourceConnection both faces extend.
Correlated query owner: checks the response's source/generation AND the result's op against the request, rejecting on either mismatch.
Bounded source buffer: overflow drops the OLDEST prefix and is reported as a sequence gap, never raised; setState refuses an oversized replacement and restores the previous value.
Exact decoders for the Host/Worker lifecycle values; a Client bootstrap whose endpoint is not ws://127.0.0.1 is refused.
Host/Worker lifecycle message types: config, boot, shutdown, ready/failure/stopped, Client bootstrap.
Single topic name cordis/tree.
The seven fetch-observation topic names.
Versioned source lifecycle frames and exact parsers that REBUILD the object; a Host source may not declare a Client capability and a capability may not repeat.
Closed non-CDP query model: one operation (cordis-tree/get) and four error codes.
The query/request and query/response envelopes.
Exact query-frame decoders, plus a partial identity parse that rejects a malformed request without timing out its caller.
Three-line re-export of the query protocol.
Closed Client Runtime command/result union; the result discriminant mirrors the command, making cross-method settlement impossible.
Runtime request/cancel/ack/response/session-closed envelopes; the ack parser is a deliberate literal copy of the cancel parser.
Exact decoder for Client Runtime commands including the four call-argument kinds.
Exact decoder for Runtime results; validateRemoteObject enforces a per-type representation matrix (exactly one of value/unserializableValue/object).
Client Console enable/disable/event envelopes; only console-api and exception events are accepted.
Three-line re-export of the Runtime wire protocol.
Read-only Client source commands: list-scripts and get-content-chunk with a source/source-map content kind.
Client source request/response/session-closed envelopes and their parsers.
Exact source decoders; chunk data must be CANONICAL base64 (regex plus a round-trip check).
Three-line re-export of the Client source protocol.
Public export surface of the realm-neutral CDP value model.
Realm-neutral backend interfaces; RealmCapability is {supported,backend}|{unsupported,reason} so a missing capability carries a reason.
The four capability lists (runtime/console/sources/debugger) describing what a realm implements.
Realm-neutral Runtime request/result shapes, generic over the handle type.
Realm-neutral RuntimeRemoteObject: a descriptor, an optional backend object reference, an optional Cordis semantic reference.
Realm-neutral property, internal-property and private-property descriptors.
Realm-neutral exception details, stack trace and call frame.
Realm-neutral Console event model and the 18 CDP console types.
Realm-neutral debugger model: locations, scopes, call frames, pause/resume/breakpoint events.
The three realm-backend identifier roles (realm id, backend object handle, script key).
Realm-neutral RuntimeScript descriptor.
Consumer-neutral tree type: carries NO object handles, registry ids or CDP ids, and the parser rejects them.
Routed snapshot wire form; a separate type from the consumer-neutral tree so stripping routing fields is a compile-time boundary.
Pure projection from routed snapshots to the consumer-neutral tree, unit-testable in isolation.
Projects live Cordis objects to a bounded snapshot; unwraps Cordis shadow wrappers, enumerates registry fibers AND event-hook contexts, prunes to the byte budget.
Realm-local live-object retention plus IDENTIFY_REALM_OBJECT_FUNCTION and realmObjectExpression, which together make an object identifiable across a wire.
The wire-safe {registryId, handle} pair and its parser.
The two registry identifier roles.
Lifecycle-driven snapshot publication, COALESCED into a microtask so a burst of mutations yields one snapshot.
Publishes each snapshot as retained STATE on the cordis/tree topic so it is replayed on reconnect.
Transport-independent CordisRuntimeTreeReader interface and a local adapter.
Query-backed adapter implementing the same reader over the typed query protocol.
Fetch-observation payload types; headers are [name,value] tuples so duplicate header names survive.
Incremental UTF-8 SSE parser: streaming decode survives a split multi-byte character and a CRLF split across chunks.
Worker bootstrap: validates workerData, reports ready/failure/stopped, refuses to run on the main thread.
Worker assembly; the Host MessagePort carries BOTH the query protocol and the source protocol, with the query envelope tried first.
HTTP discovery, the DevTools CDP socket and the token+origin-checked Client ingest socket; the bind advances past an occupied port.
Source registry: a sequence gap is a first-class protocol event answered by source/resnapshot, and a malformed frame closes only its own source.
Worker-to-Client Runtime/Console router; the Worker ACKNOWLEDGES a response before settling it, and the timeout path cancels the page-side work.
Worker router for the Client source catalog; chunkBytes derived from the frame budget with base64 expansion accounted for.
Shared cleanup delivery for a closed Worker-side Client session.
Minimal CDP request/transport types; respondToCdpRequest is the single place an async operation settles, so a rejection always becomes a -32000 envelope.
The Worker-side CDP identifier roles, with a numeric brand for the id-shaped ones.
Per-connection CDP dispatcher; releaseObject is intercepted before the Runtime domain so the DOM adapter can forget its bindings first.
Page-target scaffold answered from a synthetic dsh://host frame; CDP_METHOD_NOT_HANDLED is a symbol sentinel.
Owns one backend session per visible realm per DevTools connection; the connectionId is embedded in every allocated CDP object id.
Runtime domain routing by contextId/uniqueContextId; a dead Client context errors instead of falling back to the Host, and objects cannot cross realms.
Per-connection table mapping every realm's backend handles to connection-local CDP object ids (runtime:<connectionId>:<n>).
Exact validation of Runtime parameters; objectId and an execution context are mutually exclusive, and a call argument carries exactly one representation.
One-line re-export of RuntimeDomainSession.
Debugger domain routing each request to the script's owning realm, with a native Host fallback and the owning realm's reason on refusal.
Connection-local ScriptId route table; two realms producing the same script key is a hard error, and retired Client ids keep their reason.
Projects realm-neutral scripts and debugger events into Debugger.scriptParsed and Debugger.paused.
Exact validation of evaluateOnCallFrame and the scriptId locator.
Four-line re-export of the Debugger domain.
Read-only Cordis DOM projection: each child list is delivered ONCE so frontend node identities survive, and a node id leaving via search first pushes its unsent ancestors.
Worker-side semantic DOM projection plus the diff; BackendNodeId keys on a stable content key so it survives revisions and connections.
Three-line re-export of the Cordis DOM domain.
Projects the network store into CDP Network events; requestWillBeSent is emitted late so the resource type is known, and streamResourceContent is per-connection.
Host-only native CDP adapter; filters forwarded notifications so the shared Runtime domain keeps ownership of Console and the default context.
Worker's routed snapshot repository; a non-newer revision is ignored so a replay cannot roll the view back, and closed sources are frozen and bounded.
Registry of realm definitions; realms() returns Host first then Clients in admission order, and that order drives every connection.
Realm lifecycle model; the context is a union of native vs synthetic, making context ownership explicit.
Normalised fetch repository; the replay journal keeps lifecycle events but not per-chunk data events, and a malformed payload loses only that observation.
Query admission and bounded settlement; an oversized result is answered with result-too-large, and a malformed request is answered or the transport closed.
Executes one closed query against the shared semantic reader.
Host realm definition; openSession creates a FRESH node:inspector session per DevTools connection.
Per-connection bridge to the real V8 target; notifications are serialised through a promise chain, and a failed connect is remembered.
RuntimeBackend over the native inspector session; the native objectId is re-branded as the realm handle, and the realm is asked to identify its own objects.
ConsoleBackend over native Runtime notifications, converted to realm-neutral events.
DebuggerBackend over native Debugger notifications: paused frames, scopes, breakpoints.
SourceBackend over native scriptParsed notifications; keeps a connection-local script catalog.
Converts a native Node inspector script id into the realm's RuntimeScriptKey namespace.
Three small validators for native-protocol records and optional fields.
Client realm definition; capabilities are DERIVED from what the source declared, so a missing capability carries a reason.
The three Worker services a Client realm adapter needs, in one value.
RuntimeBackend over the typed transport; assertClientEvaluationOptions refuses the options the browser cannot honour, each with its own message.
ConsoleBackend over the Client Console subscription.
SourceBackend over the bounded Client catalog; each chunk is validated (length, monotonic offset, ceiling) before concatenation.
ClientScriptIdentity: a memoised, stable translation from Client-local script key to realm-wide RuntimeScriptKey.
Converts Client wire values into realm-neutral Runtime values (completions, properties, exceptions, Console events, stacks).
The typed "Client native debugging is unavailable" capability.
Builds lib/devtools from the pinned npm sources into a temp dir and renames it into place, emitting a size+SHA-256 integrity manifest.
Four npm source adapters; restoreModuleUrls uses the TypeScript compiler API to rewrite import.meta.url/resolve so deployment sub-paths survive, and refuses to touch strings/comments/regexes.
Locates the installed npm DevTools source, VERIFYING the version matches the pin, and generates the image CSS module.
Vite build of the DevTools frontend: Node platform swapped for browser, puppeteer/lighthouse stubbed, injected scripts built separately, connect.js emitted as an entry that loads first.
Proves the bootstrap route exists before the Worker is ready and answers 503 on failure; injects four failure kinds including a message-only mention of the platform code.
Proves the iframe key listener follows document loads and the effective binding.
Bottom panel through the production slot renderer: shortcut, iframe lifetime, pointer/keyboard resize, focus restoration, locale switch, unload.
Packs the package, extracts the tarball, and evaluates the Host from the packed artifact through plain Node.
Chromium end-to-end: real page, real DevTools frontend, node identity across expansions, Client Console forwarding, built bundle as read-only source.
Client Runtime executor's nine behaviours including per-request rollback, cancellation, provisional handles and Console session isolation.
Source catalog's map-URL resolution, bounded chunking, and load-failed/result-too-large outcomes.
Browser stack parser's 0-based normalisation and script-key association.
Proves the Client Console and Sources projections agree on ONE script key.
Proves the collector keeps a service-created Fiber distinct from its canonical Context and retains both live objects.
Exhaustive validation of both tree models, the projection, and the registry (then-wrapper walk, hostile proxy, committed-generation rejection).
Consumer-neutral projection, query codecs, correlation/timeout/close paths, Worker bounded outcomes, and a Host+Client integration; forbiddenKeys() walks the tree asserting no routing ids leak.
1204-line spec: collector budgets, observer coalescing, DOM diff, depth-limited delivery, scoped projections, and the reconnect path.
Child process with a paused Host main thread; sets a breakpoint, evaluates on the frame, and checks a Worker-local request still completes while paused.
Builds the frontend with fetch/http/https all stubbed to throw, proving no network access, and asserts the npm sources are byte-identical afterwards.
Client selection in the bootstrap and upgrade URL, including the deployment-prefix case and malformed-selector rejection.
Evaluates each source adapter in a per-test VM: import.meta rewriting, CSS text module, TimelinePanel patch, CodeMirror browser branch, image module.
Proves the disposal order and the aggregation of cleanup failures.
SSE parser across chunk, CRLF and UTF-8 boundaries.
Fourteen fetch-wrapper behaviours, including the Node-specific case where the caller's abort only reaches native fetch while the wrapper Request is reachable (forces a real GC).

808-line integration over a real Worker and Client fixture: selection scoping, context routing, per-connection object isolation, Worker deadline, Host/Client value-model parity, Console isolation, chunked source, three Network paths.
ARCHITECTURAL spec: walks the tree to assert client/ and host/ mirror each other, worker/realms/client and host mirror, shared/ imports no face, and every spec declares its face by filename.
Runs the plugin through a real Cordis Loader composition with the inspector-profile overlay.
Worker Network projection's twelve behaviours: truncation, eviction, per-connection streaming, SSE replay, capture errors, malformed payloads, per-source closing.
DevTools frontend route (405/401/302/200/404/500) and the CDP upgrade proxy, driven over real TCP socket pairs with hand-rolled WebSocket frames.
Client plugin's twenty behaviours: pagehide/pageshow, bootstrap, identity rotation, Web Locks, cancellation, queue loss, source catalog, registration failure, recovery paths.
Host plugin end-to-end, including a real CDP round trip over DSHInspector.getSources.
Proves the Worker advances past an occupied port and publishes the selected one.
Wire protocol decoders: frame rebuilding, generation isolation, sequence gaps, malformed-frame containment, and the Runtime/Console/Sources frame families.
The JSON validator's accept/reject matrix and the exact-field readers.
Source buffer's five behaviours: absorbing queue loss once, validating before enqueue, refusing oversized state, splitting frames, one in-flight batch.
Worker lifecycle readiness, crash containment and graceful stop.
Proves the package installs NO download hook and that the built frontend rather than the tooling is what ships.
Client-face fixture running in its own Worker: opens the real ClientInspectorSource and exposes twelve commands including socket pause/resume and add/remove Fiber.
Host-side controller for that fixture: starts the Worker, correlates request/response ids, exposes the commands as typed methods.
Child process whose Host main thread can be paused; prints the endpoint and waits on stdin for run/stop.
